message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (negative, so H⁻ is unstable in vacuum) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| **Physical State (298 K, 1 atm)** | State | Gas |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (−423.15 °F) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (−434.49 °F) |
| | Specific heat (gas, 1 bar) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat of vaporization | 0.449 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Speed of sound | ~1270 m s⁻¹ (at 20 °C) |
| | Refractive index | 1.000132 (visible light) |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0016 mol L⁻¹) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| | Bonding | Forms covalent bonds (H₂, H₂O, hydrocarbons), ionic bonds (NaH, CaH₂), hydrides (AlH₃, LiH) |
| | Reactivity | Highly reactive with metals, non‑metals, and oxygen; forms H₂O, H₂S, NH₃, CH₄, etc. |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (HA ⇌ H⁺ + A⁻) in aqueous solution; forms hydronium (H₃O⁺) |
| | Redox behavior | Reducing agent (e.g., H₂ + O₂ → H₂O); oxidized to H⁺ in acids |
| | Combustion | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Photochemistry | UV light can dissociate H₂ into H atoms; H₂ can absorb in the Lyman series (121.6 nm) |
| | Spectroscopy | Diatomic H₂ shows rotational, vibrational, and electronic spectra; atomic H shows Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Stable, most abundant |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable, 1 % of natural hydrogen; heavier, used in NMR, D₂O (“heavy water”) |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive (half‑life 12.32 y), β‑emitter; used in nuclear fusion research and radiolabeling |
| **Applications & Roles** | Energy carrier | Hydrogen fuel cells, rocket propellant, industrial hydrogenation |
| | Astrophysics | Main component of stars; H‑α line (656.3 nm) key in stellar spectroscopy |
| | Chemistry | Base for synthesis of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, etc. |
| | Environmental | Clean combustion produces only water; potential for green energy |
| | Materials science | Hydrides used in batteries, hydrogen storage materials |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: atomic number 1, mass ~1 u.
- **Highly reactive**: forms H₂ gas, reacts with almost all elements.
- **Multiple oxidation states**: +1 (most common) and –1 (hydride).
- **Isotopes**: protium (stable), deuterium (stable, heavier), tritium (radioactive).
- **Key physical constants**: density 0.0899 g L⁻¹, boiling point –252.9 °C.
- **Energy relevance**: fuels, batteries, and clean combustion.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
